title: The Error You Only Get When It Runs: What QML Checks, and When

questions.question: A QML file contains Item { widht: 100 }, a typo on the property name. When do you find out?
options: When the file loads: QML can read that the property does not exist, so it refuses, at line 2 column 8
When you build: moc checks QML property names
Never: unknown properties are ignored
When the item is first drawn
questions.explanation: An unknown property on a known type is visible in the document, so QML refuses the load and reports a line and a column. What it cannot check by reading is what a binding computes.

questions.question: A binding reads robto.speed, misspelling a context property named robot. What happens?
options: The file loads, the property keeps its default of 0, and the only trace is a warning nothing is connected to
The load fails with an error naming the line
The binding is skipped and the property is left unset, which QML reports as an error at first use
It resolves to an empty object, so the property becomes an empty string
questions.explanation: Whether a name resolves is not knowable by reading the file, only by running the binding. So the object is created, the interface draws, and the width is zero. QQmlEngine emits a warnings signal, and nothing is connected to it unless you connect it.

questions.question: Item { width: 0/0 } loads. How many errors and warnings does Qt report?
options: None of either: the width is 0 and nothing anywhere says so
One warning about a division by zero
One error, because NaN is not a valid width
One warning, but only in a debug build
questions.explanation: 0/0 is NaN in JavaScript, and NaN assigned to a real property becomes zero. That is legal by every definition QML has, so there is no channel to report it on. This is the tier a test has to catch, because nothing else can.

questions.question: You load a QML file with QQmlApplicationEngine and rootObjects() comes back empty. What have you been told?
options: One bit, when QQmlComponent::errors() would have given a url, a description, a line and a column
Everything available: QML reports failures as a boolean
That the file is missing, since a present file always produces a root object
That the file loaded but the root type was not a visual item
questions.explanation: QQmlComponent is the primitive underneath, and it keeps the full error list. Checking rootObjects().isEmpty() discards a line number that the engine already computed.

questions.question: Summarise when QML checks a mistake.
options: It checks what it can read in the document, and runs everything else
It checks everything at load, so a file that loads is correct
It checks nothing until the property is first read
It checks types at build time through moc, and names at load time
questions.explanation: A string literal where a number goes is refused at load. A binding that computes a string where a number goes is not, because the document does not say what the binding will produce. That one sentence predicts all twelve cases in this lesson.

questions.question: Your QmlHost loads a component that returns no root object, and component.errors() is empty. What should load() return?
options: A failure carrying one problem saying the component produced no root object
An empty error list, which accurately reflects what Qt reported
Success with a null pointer, so the caller can decide
A failure with no detail, since there is nothing truthful to add
questions.explanation: A caller handed an empty list of reasons has been told nothing, and will print an empty message. Saying that much is honest and actionable, and it is a case that happens.
